name: csharp-async
description: C# async best practices

Use the `Async` suffix; match synchronous counterparts when applicable (e.g., `GetDataAsync()` for `GetData()`). Return `Task<T>` for values, `Task` otherwise; consider `ValueTask<T>` for high-performance scenarios. Avoid `void` except event handlers. Use try/catch around await; avoid swallowing exceptions. Use `ConfigureAwait(false)` when appropriate in library code. Propagate exceptions with `Task.FromException()` instead of throwing in async Task returning methods. Use `Task.WhenAll()` for parallel tasks and `Task.WhenAny()` for timeouts/first completion. Avoid unnecessary async/await; consider cancellation tokens for long-running operations.

Never use `.Wait()`, `.Result`, or `.GetAwaiter().GetResult()` in async code. Avoid mixing blocking and async code. Don't create async void methods (except for event handlers). Always await Task-returning methods. Implement the async command pattern for long-running operations. Use async streams (`IAsyncEnumerable<T>`) for sequences; consider TAP for public APIs. When reviewing C# code, identify these issues and suggest improvements following these practices.
